title: UHI v6.1.1: facility-specific probabilistic priority lists of temperate exoplanets for JWST and ELT (code, data and Sobol N=512 sensitivity)
description:
Version 6.1.1 of the UHI code and data products: a documentation release of v6.1 (English code comments and docstrings, README corrections, and a new top-N membership analysis). The model code and every numerical output are identical to v6.1 (version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24430693). It assigns temperate exoplanets from the NASA Exoplanet Archive (pscomppars snapshot of 2026-11-18; 6,112 planets scored) a probabilistic priority for atmospheric follow-up. Ten thousand realizations per planet carry catalogue uncertainties through a smooth tidal-locking climate treatment, atmospheric retention under cumulative stellar XUV (cosmic shoreline), a per-draw rocky / Hycean / gas-rich class, and a detection model for JWST (transiting) or ELT/PCS reflected light (non-transiting). Lists are given per facility and per class.

Main numbers. Planets with a non-zero survival probability at 5σ and 3σ: 255 rocky, 71 Hycean, 287 combined.

Global sensitivity. Saltelli–Sobol, N = 512, 32 parameters, 17,408 evaluations per threshold; 95% bootstrap intervals on mean total-order indices. Rocky branch: the closing criterion is met on the half-width reading (all ten leading indices below 0.05 at both thresholds) but not on the full-width reading (9 of 10 at both thresholds). The position and width of the cosmic shoreline dominate (ST 0.22 and 0.12 at 5σ; 0.25 and 0.14 at 3σ). The Hycean branch is INDICATIVE, not converged (6 of 10 on the half-width reading and 2–3 of 10 on the full-width reading; 11 of its 17 outputs are degenerate and cannot be recovered by a larger N, while the effect of a larger N on the six retained outputs has not been tested); it is led by the H2 envelope pressure (ST 0.71).

Example use. To shortlist JWST transmission targets among likely rocky worlds, filter results/v6.1/uhi_v6_rocky_main_5s.csv to transiting planets and sort by UHI_rank; the Sobol tables then show which inputs would most change that order.

Contents: Python source with English documentation, tests, the AST check used to confirm that v6.1.1 changes no code, the top-N membership script and tables, the catalogue snapshot and auxiliary tables, per-branch results for 24 variants (12 prior and model variants at two thresholds), prior-robustness and Phase 1 check tables, Sobol outputs sufficient to regenerate the report, figures, run logs and the pinned environment. See README.md and CHANGELOG.md in the archive.

This version supersedes, but does not replace, the frozen v5.2 package (version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24358996), which remains citable on its own.

AI use: two custom LLM-based agents (Shoggothsito, implementation and execution; Aetherios, technical review) assisted under the author's direction; see docs/AI_DISCLOSURE.md for the validation steps.

License: code MIT; data, results and figures CC BY 4.0. NASA Exoplanet Archive data are public (NASA/IPAC).
